root_cause: One-shot generation with no execution feedback: empty/incorrect drafts (wrong literal values, wrong join keys, wrong projected columns) are returned unchecked
what: Add a draft-then-verify loop: execute the first SQL via env.execute and, if it errors or returns 0 rows, make a second policy call that includes the error/empty result plus sampled distinct values of the string columns referenced in the question/hint, so the model can fix literals, join keys and projections. Also strengthen the system prompt with general Spider-style conventions (select all columns for 'details'/entity questions, DISTINCT for list questions, LIKE '%text%' for substring matching, use both sides of relation tables for NOT IN).
decision: s1 delivers the largest measured gain (83.33 → 90.0) with zero broken tasks, while s2 gains less and regresses sp0600; both share the same generic execute-then-repair rationale, so s1's extra token cost is justified by its clean, higher-scoring outcome.

root_cause: Single-shot SQL is never executed; empty/erroring drafts caused by wrong join keys, wrong filter columns or wrong LIKE direction are returned unverified
what: Add an execution-verification loop: run the first draft with env.execute; if it errors or returns zero rows, gather generic diagnostics (error text, sample values of columns used in string filters) and make one repair call with the draft plus diagnostics, preferring the repaired query when it now returns rows. Also add concise output-shape/LIKE/join rules to the system prompt.

root_cause: The repair loop only fires on errors/empty results and its value sampler never inspects columns the question does not name, so wrong literals in un-named filter columns (degree_summary_name='Bachelors', Friend.student_id vs friend1) stay broken; projection width for unnamed-entity questions is also under-specified
what: Two edits: (1) solve.py now samples stored values of every text column actually used in the draft's WHERE/HAVING/ON clauses (not just question-word-matched columns), and additionally triggers one repair call when a non-empty draft filters on an exact string literal that matches no stored value in any sampled text column (NULL-safe NOT IN/NOT EXISTS excluded from the emptiness trigger). (2) system_prompt.md strengthens the projection rule (entity named without attributes -> SELECT T1.* even through joins, DISTINCT only if asked) and adds generic guidance to verify categorical/code literals against real stored values and to check both column names and directions of self-referencing relation tables.
